name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,244

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A singing duo performs a soft, gentle number.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a set of two people or things taken together as a unit.

blocks.note: the setter is 'I', so 'the setter is' becomes I'M
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: An invitation to fetch the crossword compiler's bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves as 'the setter', 'this writer' or 'me'; here the possessive-looking 's is really 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To import goods is to bring them into a country from abroad for sale or use.

clue.text: Impartial international body founded to protect India

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the UN is the United Nations
founded on something means based on it
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A neutral global organisation set up to defend India.
explanation.walkthrough: The UN fits the surface so neatly as the impartial body that it is easy to miss that it is just the first two letters; BASED then holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without bias favours no side, which is exactly what being neutral and fair-minded means.

clue.text: Fully absorbed style of music over time

blocks.note: rap is a genre of music with spoken rhyming lyrics
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone utterly lost in a musical style as the years go by.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so RAP sits on top of T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapt listener is completely engrossed, with attention wholly captured by something.

clue.text: River in spring’s sound perhaps of little interest

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
boing is the noise a spring makes when it bounces, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A river in springtime might make a sound nobody much cares about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' suggests the season next to a river, but it is the coiled metal kind that goes BOING, with R placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and tedious holds little interest, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: The middle of that poet’s musical

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, leaving off both ends

blocks.note: the two central letters of the four-letter word
John Milton wrote Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: Asking about the central part of some poet's stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking wordplay to definition. Milton is the classic crossword poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop stage show about Alexander Hamilton is a hugely successful Broadway production.

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, Latin for about
R is for rex, Latin for king
soldiers are often clued as men

explanation.surface: An opera whose plot concerns a monarch and his troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it introduces the opera's subject, but it is the abbreviation CA; the soldiers are MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's Carmen, about a Spanish gypsy and a soldier, is one of the most performed operatic works.

clue.text: In the morning, more talk endlessly lacking ethics

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a.m. means before noon
an oral is a spoken exam, so more than one is orals

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps chattering away at breakfast without any scruples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More talk' is a plural: one spoken exam is an oral, so several are orals. 'Endlessly' then trims that plural, not the word 'talk'.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoral person has no moral principles at all, so the adjective means without any sense of right and wrong.

clue.text: Somewhat fear son is turning criminal

indicators.note: somewhat means only to some extent, so just part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across these words, skipping the start and end

explanation.surface: A parent worries their boy is going to the bad.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through feAR SON IS Turning. 'Turning' looks like a reversal signal but simply supplies the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist sets fires deliberately, an offence, so the noun names one particular kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Two seconds to catch black bird

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: II is two in Roman numerals
S is the abbreviation for seconds
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: In a couple of seconds you might snare a dark-feathered bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two seconds' reads as a brief moment, but splits into Roman II and S, which then go around B.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading creature with a curved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

blocks.note: first meaning: flat cartilaginous sea fish, in the plural
second meaning: glides on blades across a frozen surface

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fish crossing ice; the word is a plural noun for the fish and a verb for gliding on blades.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat rays sold as food share their name with the verb for moving on ice on bladed boots.

indicators.note: something done horribly is badly messed up, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: kin are relatives, one's family
taken as written, ready for rearranging

explanation.surface: A tragic hero's relatives give him dreadful looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', the link. Fittingly, Shakespeare's tragedy turns on how the old king's daughters treat him.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's old monarch, betrayed by two daughters and driven mad, is a central tragic protagonist.

clue.text: Without pressure, difficult situation’s easy to bear

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
a plight is a dangerous or difficult predicament

explanation.surface: Once the stress is lifted, a tough spot becomes bearable.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P from PLIGHT leaves the answer; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light burden or punishment weighs little, so it is not hard to endure or carry.

clue.text: Lead me on, having mixed drink

indicators.note: mixed things are stirred together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone being strung along after a cocktail too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed drink' looks like a cocktail, but 'mixed' works on the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a sweet soft beverage flavoured with citrus, a familiar example of something to quench thirst.

clue.text: The first lady happening to lose books

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so letters are removed

blocks.note: an event is an occurrence
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A president's wife is at a function where she misplaces some novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's spouse, but it means the first woman in Genesis. Taking NT from EVENT leaves her name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam's partner was the earliest woman created, hence the very first female human.

clue.text: Wanderer hid among set back houses

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it within, so the letters sit inside the words
setting something back sends it the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: these letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A traveller hides among homes set back from the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set back houses' reads as homes away from the street, but it says 'reversed, contains': hiD AMONg holds the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams from place to place with no fixed home, so is a person who roves.

indicators.note: confusing things means muddling them up, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the six letters, ignoring the joining word

explanation.surface: An adult gets tea and rum mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', so the definition is adjectival 'grown-up'; 'and' just joins the two drinks in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, both describe someone fully developed and adult in body or behaviour.

indicators.note: to implicate is literally to fold in, so one piece is wrapped inside another

blocks.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
Elon Musk, the tech billionaire

explanation.surface: A memo from Italy's leader dragging a famous billionaire into something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Musk is clued by his first name, not by the perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgia Meloni became prime minister of Italy in 2022, heading its government.

blocks.note: first meaning: one who lets property
second meaning: a symbol of the alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a landlord's personality; the 's is 'is' and the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rents out property is literally someone who lets it, and an alphabet symbol is a written character.

indicators.note: a cover goes round the outside, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: the FT is the Financial Times
LA is the standard abbreviation for the city

explanation.surface: A paper's report on a home in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a London business daily, usually called the FT.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a self-contained set of rooms on one floor of a building is a dwelling of this kind.

indicators.note: changing something alters its form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A monument that will be expensive to alter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not cheap' sounds like the cost of the work, but it is the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a monument honouring war dead whose bodies lie elsewhere, a commemorative structure.

indicators.note: a revolution is a full turn, so the letters are turned round

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A good-looking policeman and a French radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer and 'French revolutionary' a historical figure, but they are CU and a French word turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cute is pretty or charming, appealing in a sweet way.

clue.text: Ask questions about closure of Yorkshire quarry

indicators.note: the closure of something is its end, so only the final letter is used
to be about something is to be around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to pry is to inquire nosily
the final letter of the county name

explanation.surface: Someone inquires why a Yorkshire stone pit was shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' looks like part of the pit's description, but it is the definition in its hunting sense. Yorkshire is a large county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarry in its hunting sense is the animal being chased, the same as a hunted victim.

blocks.note: par is the normal or expected level
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Echoing the usual nonsense without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR is the golfing standard score for a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to echo words without understanding, as the talking bird copies phrases.

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Motorists keep selling petrol now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers sell fuel' makes a neat sentence on its own, so 'Periodically' is easy to read as an adverb on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is a heavy oil burned in compression-ignition engines, a common type of motor fuel.
